summary: 80-ft steel CCC-era fire tower on Jack Mountain near Monterey, VA: dismantled in 2002, reinstalled in 2017, privately owned by Skip Jones; daylight visits reported in 2020-2021, no newer access confirmation.

facts.design: 80-foot all-steel lookout tower (planned at 47 feet, changed in 1934)
facts.status_note: Dismantled and removed in 2002 (a 2004 Recorder item gives that year), stored, then restored and reinstalled on Jack Mountain in 2017.

access.note: Privately owned. NHLR says it was left open to visitors during daylight from November 2020, and a January 2021 county piece describes daytime visits. No newer confirmation found; check with the owner before going.

visit.trail_note: Gravel drive off Sounding Knob Road, 1.3 miles south of Rt. 250; more than 100 steps to the top (VACo, 2021). Confirm access with the owner.

events.note: NHLR: built 1935 for the Virginia Department of Forestry by CCC workers. Jones and VACo say 1934; a 1934 newspaper item describes the camp and road.
Lookout watchman Jesse Wiseman moved into the tower March 11, 1948; still on duty in October 1950
Dismantled and removed from its original location on Sounding Knob. A Recorder item dated July 24, 2004 reports the dismantling.
Purchased by Hammill Skip Jones; parts then went to Highland Welding and the Virginia Department of Forestry overhaul
Totally disassembled; steel re-galvanized in Ashland, VA; bolts re-galvanized in Illinois; new hemlock steps; reinstalled on Jack Mountain
Registered July 8, 2017, nominated by Brian Powell; public dedication that day
NHLR says the tower and cab were left open to visitors during daylight hours from November 2020

corrections.proposed: Private owner: Hammill Skip Jones (built for the Virginia Department of Forestry)
corrections.why: A person is not an agency. NHLR lists Jones under 'Administered by' and says the tower is privately owned.

corrections.current: Moved a short way, to a new spot on the same site (FFLA)
corrections.proposed: Dismantled in 2002, stored, and reinstalled on Jack Mountain at Sounding Knob in 2017; distance from the first spot not stated
corrections.why: NHLR and the Allegheny Mountain Radio pieces describe dismantling and reinstallation. None of the three sources says it moved a short distance on the same site, so the FFLA wording is not confirmed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, Allegheny Mountain Radio and VACo say 2002. A Recorder item dated July 24, 2004 reports the dismantling. The story gives 2002 and notes the 2004 item.
NHLR says 1935 and Eastern's March 1935 item describes an 80-foot tower being built. Jones and VACo say 1934, and the May 1934 item describes the camp and road. The story gives both.

NHLR says it was reinstalled at Sounding Knob. VACo says it was removed from its original location and now stands on top of Jack Mountain. No source gives the distance. The story does not call it a short move.

NHLR's 2017 text says the tower is gated. Its later text says it was left open during daylight from November 2020, and VACo's January 2021 piece describes daytime visits. No newer source was found, so the level is restricted, not public.

notes_for_editor: The record name 'moved from its original spot' is not supported by the cited sources, which describe dismantling and reinstallation on Jack Mountain. The coordinates differ: the record's tower point (38.395783, -79.563883) and the separate FFLA 'Sounding Knob' point (38.34636, -79.59001) are about 6 km apart by my estimate. No source explains that gap, so it needs checking. A Highland County Chamber of Commerce directory lists 'Sounding Knob Fire Tower (Firetower LLC)', which suggests a business operator. I saw only a search snippet, so ownership and access may have changed since 2021. Elevation 1214 m is kept from the brief, not re-checked. Staffing 'until the 1960s' is a decade only, so no event year is given. Read budget: five distinct pages and two searches, close to the cap.
